messages:
jessica (support): FYI multiple customers reporting p99 spikes for text-gen endpoints since ~14:20 UTC. Several report 2-3x p99. Sample trace attached.

alex (eng-sre): Which regions/models are hitting this?

jessica (support): Mostly us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Heaviest on llama-13B-q4 and a few on 7B variants.

maria (eng-runtime): I see a correlated increase in host-side io queue depth for gen workers. Metrics show NVMe latency tail rising around 13:40 UTC. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/obs/dash/kv-cache-hostfs

dave (eng-infra): We rolled CUDA 12.2.1 + GPU FW 46.2 to parts of us-west fleet yesterday at ~13:45 UTC. Could be related to hostfs/io interaction. :eyes:

alex (eng-sre): Pulling dmesg from an affected host now.

alex (eng-sre): ```
[Mar17 13:51:02] nvme0: I/O 512 QID 12 timeout, status: 0x800
[Mar17 13:51:02] nvme: aborting command, qid=12
[Mar17 13:51:03] gpu0: nvlink: rmw stall detected
[Mar17 13:51:04] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
```

maria (eng-runtime): Also seeing host CPU sys spikes and KV cache eviction rate up ~4x. Prefix caching hitting disk more often.

jessica (support): Customer repro snippet: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"model":"llama-13B-q4","prompt":"long prompt..."}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'``` tail latency jumps to ~650ms on p99 for them.

dave (eng-infra): Quick mitigation options: mark FW 46.2 hosts as degraded in scheduler so they stop getting new gen traffic, or roll FW back on a small canary. We can also tweak nvme_io_timeout and qdepth kernel params temporarily.

alex (eng-sre): Routing rule being applied now to drain updated nodes from gen pool and route to older-firmware pool. Enabling fallback to llama-7B for critical customers while we triage. Rolling now. :rocket:

maria (eng-runtime): Routing applied. Early signals: p95 improved ~15-20%, p99 down ~30% for impacted tenants but still above baseline. Need deeper repro to confirm root cause.

dave (eng-infra): Kicking off NVMe firmware rollback on 5 canary hosts now, and scheduling a repro run comparing driver 535 vs 540 with fio random read/write 4k 70% r / 30% w at 8 threads to replicate host-side interference.

alex (eng-sre): Will also collect full trace samples (kv cache logs + kernel io trace + GPU metrics) from affected hosts. Assigning to @dave and @maria for triage.

jessica (support): Notified affected customers with ETA: we will attempt rollback canary in 60m, broader mitigation after validation. I'll post updates. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Incident INC-20260317-45 created and linked to this thread.

alex (eng-sre): Next steps: 1) validate rollback canary results 2) run controlled fio+model run to reproduce 3) if repro, coordinate FW/driver rollback plan + postmortem.

dave (eng-infra): If rollback doesn't show clear improvement, plan B is to pin scheduler to avoid combined high-concurrency workloads on same host (hotspot isolation) and tune kernel qdepth.

maria (eng-runtime): I'll prepare a short eval harness to run a steady-generation workload with KV cache warm/cold cycles to exercise eviction and disk fallback.

jessica (support): Thanks team — I'll keep customers updated and paste any additional repro logs here.
